threads.body: This package’s .changelog/.gitignore differs from the pattern used by the other instrumentation packages (they keep only `!.gitignore`). As written, these negation rules don’t have any effect unless something else ignores the directory, and they add inconsistency across packages. Aligning with the existing pattern makes the changelog setup easier to reason about.

This PR introduces a new instrumentation package, but it doesn’t include the required minimal examples under `examples/manual/` and `examples/zero-code/` (per .github/instructions/instrumentation.instructions.md). Even if operation patching comes later, having runnable examples is part of the package boilerplate expected in this repo.

replies.body:
@lmolkova Yes, CrewAI has its own native OpenTelemetry instrumentation and it's not aligned with GENAI semantic conventions.

I felt adding OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions to native library is a larger effort as CrewAI is currently focused adding additional telemetry as per conventions. Here is the open PR https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/6304.

Additionally while I was researching around the implementation I saw LangChain and LangGraph also provide native tracing through LangSmith but we have GENAI aligned instrumentation here. Because of these reasons I felt adding genai aligned instrumentation is better here.

However I am not completely sure about the opentelemetry best practices. If you feel we should work with crewai to get genai semantic conventions in their sdk I can open up an issue and work with them. Let me know your thoughts.

thanks for the context @venkata-pavani ! Trying crewai out, it indeed seems very far from OTel GenAI semconv and doesn't even propagate context properly so that underlying OpenAI instrumentation is not correlated. The fact that https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/6304 sits there for a month without any comments is a good indication that it's not a priority for crewai. I think this is a good justification to provide instrumentation here. Could you please still create an issue in crewAI and point to this PR and this repo and kindly ask crewai folks to reach out if they want to adopt conventional instrumentation?

thanks @venkata-pavani ! one more question: is crewai native instrumentation enabled by default? is there a way for us to disable it when this instrumentation is enabled? We can support an option to keep their telemetry coming too, but not by default.
